description:
I'm an IT student interested in web development, technology, and space exploration. I'm participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 with my project Sol One, an interactive lunar mission simulator for children.

I enjoy learning new skills, building creative projects, and solving problems. I'm passionate about turning ideas into reality through technology.

I'm currently participating solo and would love to connect with people interested in web development, UI/UX design, game development.
summary:
Sol One is an interactive lunar outpost management and astronaut training web application built with React 19, Vite, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, and Express, utilizing NASA open data. It simulates real-time lunar station survival, allowing users to balance power generation, life support systems, hydroponic food production, and radiation shielding across lunar Sols.
  The application tackles space exploration complexities by turning real aerospace hurdles into an interactive experience. It addresses environmental hazards—such as unexpected solar flares, power drops, and cosmic radiation—by letting users execute real-time operational decisions, assign crew members to critical tasks, and upgrade outposts like Solar Arrays and Storm Shelters. As humanity advances toward sustainable lunar habitation through initiatives like Artemis, preparing future space engineers and explorers is essential. Sol One bridges complex space science with immersive education, making vital resource management and engineering trade-offs engaging and accessible for off-world survival.
details:
​What does your project do, and how does it work?

Sol One is an interactive lunar outpost management and astronaut training web application. It simulates real-time space station survival where users manage critical resources like power generation, life support systems, hydroponic food production, and radiation shielding across lunar Sols. It works by processing dynamic telemetry data and letting users make operational decisions, handle sudden hazards (like solar flares), and assign crew tasks.

​What benefits does it have?

It provides an engaging, hands-on learning environment for understanding complex space station mechanics, resource allocation, and emergency response management without real-world risks.

​What is the intended impact?

To inspire and train the next generation of space explorers and engineers by making aerospace concepts, off-world survival challenges, and mission planning accessible and educational.

​What tools did you use?

Built using React 19, Vite, Three.js, Tailwind CSS, and Express, integrated with official NASA open data to ensure authenticity.

​How is your project creative?

It uniquely combines 3D graphics (Three.js) and gamified simulation mechanics with real NASA datasets, transforming dry technical data into an immersive, interactive astronaut training game.

​What factors did your team consider?

We focused on real-world constraints of lunar habitation—such as extreme radiation exposure, solar power volatility, life support limitations, and efficient crew workload distribution under emergency conditions.
